standards_review.notes: All 5 commit subjects match EPMCDME-####: Description format: Add router-level tests; Add _expand_project_rows; Add dual-marker freshness latch; Extract get_user_project_spend_rows; Add batched reset-cutoff method.
License headers and from __future__ present; modern unions used. Violation: bare list[dict] at lines 49, 55, 196, 239 in member_spend_service.py; code-quality.md requires list[dict[str, Any]].
No credential logging; auth dependencies not modified. SQL uses ORM-parameterised expressions; f-string in text() at :485 uses only an internal constant, not user input. No issues found.

findings.title: Fragile BudgetCategory suffix lookup without fallback
findings.problem: _CATEGORY_SUFFIX is indexed directly with category.value inside _expand_project_rows. The map has exactly 3 keys matching the current enum members; any future BudgetCategory addition absent from the map raises KeyError. Reachability uncertain — the iteration is over the live enum and the code path is reachable from the personal page endpoint.
findings.impact: Adding a fourth BudgetCategory crashes _expand_project_rows for every user on the personal page until the map is patched.
findings.recommendation: Replace _CATEGORY_SUFFIX[category.value] with _CATEGORY_SUFFIX.get(category.value, f' ({category.value})') to degrade gracefully on unknown categories.

findings.title: Unhandled exception in project rows path kills budget response
findings.problem: get_user_project_spend_rows is awaited at lines 366-368 without any try/except; a DB error, broken connection, or any exception propagates unhandled and aborts get_budget_usage entirely.
findings.impact: A transient project-spend failure denies the user their personal budget data, returning a 500 on the analytics endpoint even when personal data is available.
findings.recommendation: Wrap lines 366-368 in try/except Exception, log a warning, and fall back to project_rows = [] so personal budget data is always returned.

findings.title: Bare list[dict] annotations violate parameterized generics rule
findings.problem: _category_columns is annotated -> list[dict], local variable columns typed list[dict] (line 55), and the return types of get_user_project_spend and get_project_member_spend include list[dict] in their tuple annotations (lines 196, 239). code-quality.md requires parameterized generics.
findings.impact: Partially-met blocking code-quality standard; dict left unparameterised loses element-type checking and fails the commit-quality gate.
findings.recommendation: Replace every list[dict] in this file with list[dict[str, Any]]; Any is already imported from typing.

findings.title: Failed refresh silences retries via unconditional latch in finally
findings.problem: _last_checked_at is set in the finally block (lines 317-318) regardless of whether _refresh_all_member_spend succeeded or raised. The exception is caught and logged, but the latch is still armed.
findings.impact: A failed provider call marks the data as fresh, suppressing all retry attempts for the full TTL; project member spend stays stale until the latch expires.
findings.recommendation: Move self._last_checked_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc) into the try block after _refresh_all_member_spend returns successfully, and remove it from the finally block.

findings.title: Missing call-order assertion: project rows fetched before _load_from_db
findings.problem: test_get_budget_usage_personal_rows_first_then_project verifies output ordering but does not assert that get_user_project_spend_rows is awaited before _load_from_db. The spec explicitly names this call-order assertion as required.
findings.impact: A call-ordering regression — such as inserting a _load_from_db call before the project rows fetch — could go undetected; expire_on_commit would then silently invalidate project row ORM objects.
findings.recommendation: Add a call-sequence assertion via assert_awaited sequence inspection or a side_effect ordering hook confirming get_user_project_spend_rows is awaited before _load_from_db.

findings.title: Missing test: all-categories-skipped project emits no rows
findings.problem: No test constructs a project_spend_rows entry where platform=0/None, cli=0/None, premium=0/None; the all-skip path of _expand_project_rows is unexercised. The spec explicitly requires this scenario.
findings.impact: A regression in the limit/spend skip guard for the all-empty case would go undetected, potentially leaking zero-spend project rows into the personal page response.
findings.recommendation: Add a test with a project having limit=None and spend=0 for all three categories and assert _expand_project_rows returns no rows for that project while rows for other projects are unaffected.
